subject: Copywriting
title: The First Marketing Email
description: A short lesson to help you apply The First Marketing Email.

hook.text: In 1978, Gary Thuerk sent one email to 400 people on ARPANET. It sold $13 million in computers. Also created spam.

buildup.text: Thuerk worked for Digital Equipment Corporation. His mass email pitched new computers to ARPANET users directly.

discovery.text: The response was explosive: orders poured in. But so did complaints. The Defense Department threatened to ban him.

twist.text: That single email had a 3,250% ROI. Modern email marketing averages $36 per $1 spent. Thuerk discovered a goldmine.

climax.text: One email created an industry worth $11 billion today.

punchline.text: $13 million from one email. Email marketing was born in 1978.

quiz.question: How much did the first marketing email generate in sales?

details.summary: The first marketing email was sent in 1978 by Gary Thuerk of Digital Equipment Corporation to 400 ARPANET users, promoting DEC computers. It generated $13 million in sales and is considered both the birth of email marketing and the first spam message ever sent.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the origin of email marketing reveals why the channel remains the highest-ROI digital marketing tool despite being nearly 50 years old. The tension between opportunity and intrusion has defined the medium since day one.
takeaways: Gary Thuerk sent the first marketing email in 1978 to 400 recipients
The email generated $13 million in sales for DEC computers
It was simultaneously the first successful email blast and the first spam

faq.question: Why is the 1978 DEC email considered both marketing and spam?
faq.answer: The email was unsolicited and sent to hundreds of people who did not ask for it — the definition of spam. But it was also a genuine product announcement that generated massive sales. This duality has defined email marketing ever since: valuable to some, intrusive to others.

faq.question: How has email marketing evolved since 1978?
faq.answer: From mass blasts to personalized, segmented, automated campaigns. Laws like CAN-SPAM and GDPR now regulate consent. Despite predictions of its death, email consistently delivers the highest ROI of any digital channel — roughly $36 for every $1 spent.
